Dubbed the Triangle Big Muff because of the layout of its Volume, Sustain and Tone controls, this is the one that started it all. The new EHX Triangle Big Muff is a faithful re-creation of the original circa 1969 circuit now housed in a pedalboard friendly, die-cast chassis. Electro-Harmonix founder, Mike Matthews, says: “The Big Muff Pi is the pedal we are best known for so I wanted to commemorate EHX’s 50th Anniversary (1968-2018) by re-releasing V1, the very first Big Muff. Specs, tone recipes, and buying guide inside. admin 22 September 2026 21 min read Updated 26 September 2026 GG-ARTICLE-TOP There is a moment in the late summer of 1969 — Woodstock just finished, the counterculture at its peak — where a young guitarist walks into Manny’s Music on West 48th Street in New York City and picks up one of the first pedals Electro-Harmonix has ever placed in a retail store. That guitarist is Jimi Hendrix. He takes the Big Muff home. Shortly after, Mike Matthews — EHX founder — gets an invitation to hang out at a recording session. When he arrives, the Big Muff is sitting on the floor, plugged in. That is a primary-source confirmation from the man who built the pedal and witnessed the scene, documented in a Guitar World feature published September 2020. It does not get more authoritative than that. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The pedal on that floor was what we now call the Triangle Big Muff Pi: the original V1 circuit, named for the triangular layout of its three knobs — Volume, Sustain, Tone — arranged in a wide arc across a simple metallic chassis with plain black lettering. No ram’s head graphic. No color scheme. Just the circuit that started one of the longest-running fuzz dynasties in guitar history. EHX reissued this original circuit in 2018 to mark the company’s 50th anniversary. Mike Matthews himself explained the decision: “The Big Muff Pi is the pedal we are best known for so I wanted to commemorate EHX’s 50th Anniversary by re-releasing V1, the very first Big Muff. Original pedals are now selling for hundreds of dollars and this reissue absolutely nails that creamy, violin-like sustain and musical tone at a price a working musician can afford.” The Triangle Big Muff Pi reissue lives in the same compact nano-sized die-cast chassis used across EHX’s current lineup, with the same analog circuit inside and one key modern upgrade: true bypass switching. This is the one that started it all. Jump to the Rig ↓ How to Get the Tone ↓ The First Muff: From Workshop to Woodstock (1969–1972) The Big Muff Pi did not appear from nowhere. Mike Matthews had been working with fuzz circuits since the late 1960s, having taken over Guild’s Foxey Lady fuzz production — a two-transistor design — and selling it through Electro-Harmonix from 1968. But the Foxey Lady was a relatively simple circuit with limited sustain range. What Matthews wanted next was something richer, more sustained, more controllable.
